prompt:
Write a three.js ES module: export function buildCampus(THREE, opts, kit) -> THREE.Group, the ground and scenery of a miniature campus map for a classical uptown New York university, 64 wide (x from -32 to 32) by 40 deep (z from -20 to 20). Four special buildings will be placed by the host on four empty paved plots, so leave them clear: each plot is 9 by 8, centred at (-20, 0, -8), (20, 0, -8), (-20, 0, 9), (20, 0, 9), drawn as pale stone paving with a darker edge, each with a path to the centre. On the north side of the centre the landmark: a domed neoclassical library about 9 high with a colonnade and very wide stone steps and a small seated bronze statue on the steps, facing a long central lawn with crossing brick paths, hedges and a sundial; on the south side a long colonnaded library facade about 5 high. Around them, in softer slightly desaturated colours so the four special buildings stand out, symmetrical red-brick halls with copper-green roofs and limestone trim (each 4 to 7 high), iron gates on the south edge, a street with a bus shelter beyond the gates. Cherry and plane trees as rounded canopies on trunks (InstancedMesh), lamp posts with light blue banners, benches, bike racks. Also export const PLOTS = { library: [-20, 0, -8], clubs: [20, 0, -8], commons: [-20, 0, 9], career: [20, 0, 9] }, export const HOME = [0, 0, 15], and export const WALKWAYS: for each plot name an array of [x, z] points forming a path from HOME to just in front of that plot along the paths. opts = { accent } (banner colour, default light blue).

STYLE (the same as the dorm-room diorama the player already knows): a refined, cozy, stylised 3D miniature like a premium life-sim game. Smooth, rounded forms (bevelled boxes, lathe shapes, extruded bezier shapes with bevels; no raw sharp boxes), believable architecture, small secondary details, warm colours. MeshStandardMaterial with thoughtful roughness; castShadow and receiveShadow on meshes. Windows are inset panes with frames; lit windows use a warm emissive colour. Paint brick, stone, roof tiles, wood and paving as textures in code with kit.canvasTexture(width, height, (ctx, w, h) => {...}) (it returns a THREE.CanvasTexture; set wrap and repeat yourself). No text, no letters, no logos.

RULES: a plain ES module; no imports; no globals: THREE and kit arrive as arguments and are passed on to helpers. No document, window, fetch or storage. Units: 1 unit = about 3 metres of campus, Y up. Keep the triangle count moderate (under about 40,000) by reusing geometries and materials and by using InstancedMesh for repeated things such as windows, trees and lamp posts. Keep the module under 1,200 lines. Return only the code in one ```js block.
